verdicts.reason: With pooling and assume_role enabled, base.py:231 and :380-381 configure each new pooled connection through ops.compose_sql(), whose psycopg_any.py:20-22 opens the Django wrapper's cursor before base/base.py:256 has assigned the checked-out connection, causing another pool checkout during configuration; incidence was not measured without PostgreSQL.

If an alias has opened its pool before test setup, base/creation.py:64-66 returns the wrapper connection and changes NAME while postgresql/base.py:208-241 retains the alias's original pool and connection parameters, so the migration at creation.py:78-83 can target the original database; incidence was not measured without PostgreSQL.

If a request commits a session-level SET ROLE or search_path and another checkout receives the same physical connection, postgresql/base.py:228-233 installs no reset callback and :395 returns it to the pool, whose installed psycopg_pool 3.3.3 _reset_connection only rolls back active transactions unless a reset callback is set; incidence was not measured without PostgreSQL.

For OPTIONS['pool'] = {}, the falsy check at postgresql/base.py:204-206 returns None despite docs/ref/databases.txt:255-258 specifying that a dict enables a pool with those options, so this documented configuration does not use pooling.
